# Open a pull request

Options: $ARGUMENTS

## 1. Check the branch is ready

- Find the base branch (from the options, or `main`/`master`/`develop`). If the current branch is the base
  branch, stop and tell the user.
- Uncommitted changes: list them and suggest `/commit` first.
- Collect the work: `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD` and `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`.
- Find linked requirement, story or bug IDs in the branch name and commits, and read them.

## 2. Write the description

```
## Summary
What changed and why, in 2-4 sentences.

## Linked work
REQ / US / BUG IDs and tracker links.

## Changes
- Grouped by area, one line each.

## How it was tested
Commands actually run and their results; manual checks done. Never claim tests you didn't run.

## Risks and rollback
What could break; database or config changes; how to roll back.

## Checklist
Items from docs/sdlc/07-release-process.md (or: tests added, docs updated, no secrets).
```

If the branch has no tests run yet, offer to run them with the `test-runner` agent first.

## 3. Create it after confirmation

Show the title and description and wait for the user to confirm. Then push the branch if needed (Claude Code
will ask for permission) and create the pull request with `gh pr create --base <base> --title … --body …`.
If the GitHub CLI isn't installed, or the project uses GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps, give the user the
text to paste instead.
